answer.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6% QoQ. Memory_31 and memory_86 both demonstrate that simplification and shortening onboarding workflows drive measurable activation and completion improvements. Verifying these two archived sources validates the core mechanism before deploying. While memory_73 addresses the competitor's pricing pressure, activating more of our existing funnel is a faster lever than matching aggressive pricing—we risk margin compression and discount dependency. Promotional pricing is also reactive; simplifying onboarding addresses our own operational decline and can move faster than sales-assist at scale. A standard experiment isolating onboarding reduction will clarify whether the 4% completion drop is reversible through UX, and should improve activation as a downstream effect. This preserves our revenue quality over discount-driven volume.
